analysis: Integration pass over a documentation-only PR. It adds changelog.d/base-reward-zero-reason.md and docs/provider/base-rewards.md, a nav link in docs/README.md:15, a pointer in hardware-requirements.md, a note in quickstart.md (around head lines 242-243), and a 'Missing base reward' section plus a see-also link in troubleshooting.md. No code, protocol, key custody, attestation, authorization, encryption, cache or fan-helper behavior changes. TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-009, TB-010 and TB-011 and the related threats are therefore untouched. The new text is conservative and consistent with T-052, T-056 and T-058. It states that a green doctor and local billing rows are not coordinator base_reward grants, and that the last-public floor table is a snapshot and not deployed policy. base-rewards.md steps 5 and the Troubleshooting table tell operators to use `darkbloom report` and `--dry-run` first, and to avoid pasting hostnames, serials, provider keys or tokens into public issues. This is a reasonable privacy control. It cites public GitHub issues 878, 1601 and 1553 for context, which is only a mild hygiene concern if operators ignore the warning. The page says the report uploads the App Attest snapshot and system logs. The report's actual contents and retention are outside the supplied evidence. TB-002 notes report log redaction and bounded DeviceCheck observations, so no exception is implied. Cited source files (DoctorRunner.swift, DesktopAccountEarnings.swift) and the external immutable engine.go and alloc.go links were not supplied for verification. Backend reward logic is platform-owned and out of scope. Replay was incomplete (10 omitted units), but the omitted material is not part of any primary changed security surface. No security regression identified.
